'''Marco Malvaldi''' (born 27 January 1974, in [[Pisa]]) is an Italian<ref>Cf. [http://archiviostorico.corriere.it/2010/agosto/17/Malvaldi_chimico_romanziere_ultima_rivelazione_co_8_100817057.shtml Biographical Interview], on [[Il Corriere della Sera]] {{in lang|it}} URL accessed on 3 December 2012</ref> [[crime writer]].

==Short biography==
Marco Malvaldi is an [[Italians|Italian]] chemist and novelist, who began his writing career in 2007 with his first mystery story ''La [[briscola]] in cinque'' (''Game for Five'', 2014), published by the Italian [[Enzo Sellerio|Sellerio Editore]] and featuring Massimo, the ''[[barista]]'' and owner of the cleverly named BarLume ("Bar Light", also a wordplay for "flicker, glimmer of light")  who is forced into the role of investigator in the fictional [[seaside resort]] town of Pineta, along the [[Tuscany|Tuscan]] coast. He followed up by other episodes in the series: ''Il gioco delle tre carte'' (2008, transl. ''[[Three-card Monte]]'', 2014), ''Il re dei giochi (The King of Games)'' (2010), ''La carta più alta (The Highest Card)'' (2012).<ref>Cf. [http://italicissima.com/2012/09/26/marco-malvaldi/ Author's Biography] on ''Italicissima.com''. URL accessed on 3 December 2012</ref> Another novel of his,  ''Odore di chiuso (The Scent of Must)'' (Sellerio, October 2011), a [[historical mystery]] with the renowned [[Romagna]] [[gastronomy|gastronomist]] [[Pellegrino Artusi]] as the amateur detective in 19th century Italy, was awarded the ''Isola d’[[Elba]] Award'' and the [[Castiglioncello]] Prize. This book was published in [[English language|English]] under the title ''The Art of Killing Well'' (2014). In October 2011, Malvaldi also published a guidebook about his own hometown [[Pisa]], with the title ''Scacco alla Torre ([[Checkmate]] to the Tower)'' (Felici Editore): one of the book's first stories is ''Finalmente soli (Finally Alone)'', narrating of a nocturnal walk, inspired by an image taken by professional [[photographer]] Nicola Ughi, Malvaldi's official [[portraitist]] and fellow citizen; the book was presented at the ''Pisa Book Festival''.<ref>Cf. [http://www.felicieditore.it/index.php?pagina=news&id=700&blocco=34|titolo=Rassegna stampa "La Pisa di Malvaldi sul Tirreno"], on ''Felici Editore''. URL accessed on 3 December 2012</ref> 
[[File:Racconto Malvaldi-1.jpg|thumb|The image of [[Pisa]] by night, which inspired the story ''Finalmente soli''.]]

The four books composing the ''BarLume'' series have the same characters in each episode: the ''[[barrista|barista]]'' Massimo, the four aged regular patrons (Massimo's grandfather Ampelio, Aldo, Rimediotti, and Del Tacca – often speaking in the local [[Tuscany|Tuscan]] dialect), obtuse Inspector Fusco, and sexy bar assistant Tiziana.<ref>Cf. [http://archiviostorico.corriere.it/2010/agosto/17/Malvaldi_chimico_romanziere_ultima_rivelazione_co_8_100817057.shtml "Malvaldi, il chimico-romanziere - L' ultima rivelazione di Elvira Sellerio"], on  ''[[Corriere della Sera]]'' URL accessed on 3 December 2012</ref> At end of October 2012, Malvaldi published a mystery thriller, ''Milioni di milioni (Millions of Millions)'' (2012), set in the fictional Tuscan town of Montesodi Marittimo, and with its main personages an odd couple of investigators – a university [[geneticist]] and a female [[archivist]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sellerio.it/it/catalogo/Milioni/Malvaldi/5342 |title=Milioni di milioni|author=Marco Malvaldi |date= 2012 |website=sellerio.it |publisher=Sellerio |access-date=21 May 2015 |language= italian |quote=Milioni di milioni è un’investigazione all’inglese basata su labili indizi messi in fila con paziente intelligenza; ma l’ambientazione è toscana, spaccona e popolaresca, come gli altri gialli del creatore dei vecchietti del BarLume.}}</ref>

In July 2013 he was awarded the Italian literary prize ''"Premio letterario La Tore [[Isola d'Elba]]"''.<ref>[http://www.premiolatoreisoladelba.it/vincitori.html La Tore Isola d'Elba Official Website], List of Winners (by year).</ref>

Malvaldi has also authored  books of popular science. His book ''Le due teste del tiranno. Metodi matematici per la libertà'' (namely, ''The Two Heads of the Tyrant. Mathematical Methods for the Freedom'') (2017) won the third edition (2018) of Premio Asimov.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.premio-asimov.it/edizioni/edizione-2018/|title=Terza Edizione premio Asimov per l'editoria scientifica divulgativa|date=2025-09-07}}</ref><ref>{{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201130235018/https://home.infn.it/it/comunicazione/news/2871-helen-czerski-e-marco-malvaldi-vincono-ex-aequo-il-premio-asimov-2018|date=2020-11-30}} (Asimov award) for the best book in scientific dissemination published in Italy, in ex aequo with Helen Czerski's ''Storm in a Teacup.''</ref>

He is married to Samantha Bruzzone, with whom he wrote some children's stories and two novels with her: ''Chi si ferma è perduto'' (2022) e ''La regina dei sentieri'' (2024).
